public_rationale: On February 27, 2025, OpenAI attributed GPT-4.5's improvements over GPT-4o to scaling unsupervised learning [e1]. It reported GPQA scores of 71.4% for GPT-4.5 and 53.6% for GPT-4o [e1]. This company-reported alternative to additional inference-time reasoning predates the August 25, 2025 claim and contradicts its assertion that reasoning models were the only route to improved performance [e1].
limitations: The performance results and attribution to unsupervised scaling come from OpenAI; the packet provides no independent replication.
The reported comparisons do not establish improvement on every task or superiority to the strongest reasoning models.
The evidence does not isolate every training change through controlled ablations.

our_interpretation: Read efficacy as measurable task performance, including accuracy, instruction following, and successful coding.
The word only excludes meaningful improvements in new non-reasoning models achieved through training rather than additional inference-time reasoning.

The retrospective phrase have been able to covers improvements achieved by publication. No starting date is supplied, so the target period has an open beginning; recent 2025 releases can test the assertion.
criteria.support_condition: Available evaluations show that meaningful improvements in new models required additional inference-time reasoning, with no demonstrated improvements from non-reasoning model development.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one new non-reasoning model demonstrably improves on its predecessor through training or another method that does not require extra inference-time reasoning.
